events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
This is an NS-0 rider-cancelled dispute: the trip was cancelled by the driver at 14:26:55 with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record [F5], so the fee stands only if the driver's no-show case satisfies NS-1 [NS-0, NS-1]. Elements (i) and (ii) are settled in the driver's favour: the driver himself tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 and the record places the car 39 m from the pickup at that moment, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F7][F2][NS-1]. Both advocates concede this (rider rebuttal to D1/D2; driver D1/D2) [F7][F3][NS-1].

The decisive element, NS-1(iii), requires continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes until cancellation, and the trace marks this element ✗: the GPS trace has a 200-second hole between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 [F1], which is longer than 2 minutes and can be more than twice the trace's normal sampling interval, so the wait cannot be inferred across it [NS-1]. The driver's answer that F4 shows a stationary car 39 m from the pickup from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55 [F4] does not close the hole: F4 is a single start-and-end pair of samples whose end sample lies after the gap, so it does not provide independent sampling inside 14:23:25–14:26:45 [F1][F4][NS-1]. Under NS-1 a hole of this kind means the wait may not be read as continuous and the case goes to a human, and the driver's post-trip written statement that he "waited over 3 minutes" is a statement, not a record, so it cannot fill the hole [F13][NS-1].

The remaining facts do not resolve it either way: the driver messaged an arrival notice at 14:22 and a pre-cancellation notice at 14:26 on a complete, timestamped thread [F10][F11][F12], but nothing in the record shows those messages were read by the rider, and notice sent is not notice received [F10][F11][F12][NS-1]; the rider's "I came downstairs a minute after he cancelled" appears only in the complaint, not in any fact [F5][NS-1]; traffic and weather facts are irrelevant to the wait question [F14][F15][F16][NS-1]. Profile facts cannot decide the case (rider clean at F17, driver with one upheld no-show dispute at F18), and in any event F18 alone does not meet the RD-6 condition because the profile is an add-on ground only and the underlying route-deviation branch is not in play [F17][F18][RD-6].

Because the wait element cannot be settled from the record and it changes the outcome (the $6.61 fee either stands or falls), the case must go to a person rather than be decided on inference; no amount is computed [F1][F4][F5][NS-1, NS-2]. The evidence gap is exactly the unsampled stretch of the wait [F1][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Human review: verify whether the driver's "I'm Here" wait ran continuously to 14:26:55 by pulling raw/second-source telemetry for 14:23:25–14:26:45; if the wait cannot be shown, refund the $6.61 cancellation fee under NS-2, else let it stand. No account flag either way (F7 shows the tap was made in range, so the NS-2 fraud flag does not attach; F18 alone cannot carry an RD-6 flag).

Accepted as the ground for escalation, not for refund_full: F1's hole means NS-1(iii) cannot be established from the record, so the case goes to a human rather than to a decision for the rider [F1][F7][F8][NS-1, NS-2].

Accepted that F3/F4 show presence and a stationary car rather than a measured continuous wait, but this supports escalation, not a refund: the record neither shows nor excludes a workable wait [F3][F4][F1][NS-1].

Not executed: NS-2's refund is triggered only if an NS-1 element fails, and that element is undetermined, not failed, here [F1][F7][F8][NS-1, NS-2]; and F18 (one upheld no-show dispute in 90 d) is a profile fact that may only support an add-on action, and the NS-2 fraud flag is expressly ruled out because F7 places the tap 39 m from the pickup [F18][F7][NS-2, RD-6].

Rejected: F4 is a single stationary block whose end sample lies after the F1 hole, so it does not supply independent proof of presence during 14:23:25–14:26:45 [F4][F1][NS-1].

Accepted only in part: the NS-2 mismeasurement flag correctly does not attach because F7 shows the tap in range [F7][NS-2], but F18 as a profile fact cannot by itself validate the fee or decide the case [F18][NS-1].

ruling.evidence_gap: GPS trace has a hole of 200 s during the post-tap wait: no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 [F1], so the continuous wait to the 14:26:55 cancellation required by NS-1(iii) cannot be measured [NS-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: NS-1(iii) cannot be established from the record: the GPS trace has a 3 min 20 s hole (14:23:25–14:26:45) covering the end of the wait up to the 14:26:55 driver cancellation [F1][F5], and the stationary block F4 straddles that same hole rather than filling it [F4][F1]. No SAFE-1 issue found (messages F10, F11, statement F13 and traffic facts F14/F15 contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving content). No account flag: F7 shows the tap was made 39 m from the pickup, so the NS-2 fraud flag does not attach, and F18 alone cannot support an RD-6 flag.

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied on the records (F7).
The GPS trace has no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, a 3 min 20 s gap that spans almost the whole post-tap wait and ends 10 s before the 14:26:55 cancellation (F1, F5).

A gap of 3 min 20 s is more than 2 minutes and longer than double the trace's normal sampling interval, so NS-1(iii)'s continuous-waiting element cannot be established from the record and the case must go to a human, not be decided on the driver's account alone (F1, F7).

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited over 3 minutes" is contradicted by the system record of a 3 min 20 s GPS gap, and statements lose to system records, so it cannot carry NS-1(iii) (F1, F13).

The chat holds only the driver's 14:22 arrival note and his 14:26 cancellation notice, both timestamped, and the rider sent nothing; the rider was given no earlier warning that a cancellation was coming (F10, F11, F12).

The driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 14:21:15 and accumulated 5 min 40 s inside that radius before cancelling, but he was stationary 39 m away from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55; the record shows presence and a stationary car, not that the rider was given a workable wait (F3, F4).

If the no-show fee is not upheld, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full, and the driver's own record of one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days supports sending his account for review as a repeat (F8, F18).
The rider's account is 3.2 years old with a 4.5 rating and no upheld disputes, and the $6.61 fee at issue was charged on a cancellation by the driver before any trip was completed (F5, F8, F17).

weaknesses: The driver's tap at 14:22:15 was 39 m from the pickup point and he then stayed inside 200 m, so on the raw timeline the wait looks long enough; the driver will rely on F7 ("stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap") and F3 to argue NS-1(iii) is met and my client simply never came down.

The driver messaged at 14:22 (F10) that he was at the pickup point and messaged again at 14:26 (F11) before cancelling, so he will argue the rider had clear notice and chose not to appear; the rider's "I came down a minute later" story appears only in the complaint, not in any fact.

The GPS-gap argument is double-edged: the gap rule treats gaps as not presumed in anyone's favour, so the judge may read the missing 14:23:25–14:26:45 samples as neutral rather than as a defect in the driver's case, and no fact states the trace's normal sampling interval, which I must assume to apply the gap test.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 (F7), so arrival was confirmed by the driver's own tap, satisfying NS-1(i).
At the moment of the tap the driver was 39 m from the pickup point (F7), well inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1(ii) is satisfied.
After the tap the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 40 s (F7), more than the 3:01 continuous wait NS-1(iii) requires.

The driver was stationary 39 m from the pickup from 14:21:55 until cancellation at 14:26:55 (F4) and had been within 200 m since 14:21:15, a cumulative 5 min 40 s (F3, F6) — a genuine continuous wait, not a drive-by.

The driver notified the rider in-app at 14:22 ("I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6", F10) and again at 14:26 ("More than 3 min already, I have to cancel", F11) before cancelling at 14:26:55 (F5).

The rider's own complaint that she arrived "a minute after he cancelled" places her at the pickup after 14:26:55 (F5), i.e. after the driver had already waited five stationary minutes (F4); the wait period had expired before she appeared, so the $6.61 cancellation fee was properly charged (F8).
No GPS or chat fact records any threat, harassment or dangerous driving by the driver (F10, F11, F14, F15), so no SAFE escalation is warranted.

There was no abuse of the "I'm Here" button — the driver was genuinely within range when he tapped it (F2, F7) — so no flag_account may be attached under NS-2, and the driver's profile shows his prior no-show dispute was decided on the same record (F18).

weaknesses: F1: the GPS trace has no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (3 min 20 s), so the final stretch of the wait is not directly sampled; the rider will argue NS-1(iii) cannot be shown from sampling alone and that the case should go to a human under G12.

The F1 gap is longer than the normal sampling interval, so the rider may say the record cannot establish an unbroken wait up to the moment of cancellation; our answer is F4 (stationary 14:21:55–14:26:55) and F3 (5 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m), but the gap is a real evidentiary hole.

F6 vs F7 records arrival twice (platform at 14:21:15, driver's tap at 14:22:15), so the rider can argue the driver was only on station for 4 min 40 s after the tap — which still exceeds 3:01, but it invites a dispute over which timestamp governs.
Nothing in the chat (F10, F11) shows the messages were read, so the rider can say she was never told the driver had arrived; that does not defeat NS-1, but it colours the fairness of the $6.61.
The rider's profile is clean (F17: 0 disputes upheld in 90 days) against the driver's F18 (1 no-show dispute upheld), which the rider will use on credibility.

points.response: Conceded: F7 shows the driver himself tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15, so NS-1(i) is met by a driver tap, not a platform auto-arrival.
Conceded: at the tap the driver was 39 m from the pickup and had been within 200 m since 14:21:15, so NS-1(ii) is satisfied on F7 and F3.

Contested in part: F7 gives 4 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap, but NS-1(iii) requires a continuous wait "直至取消" (until cancellation), and F1 shows no samples at all between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, so the final 3 min 20 s up to the 14:26:55 cancellation is unsampled and the continuous element cannot be established from the record.

F4 shows the car stationary 39 m from the pickup for 14:21:55–14:26:55, but that same fact is a 5-minute stationary block that straddles the F1 sampling gap, so it is a single start-and-end pair, not independent proof of an unbroken presence; under NS-1 a gap longer than 2 minutes means the wait may not be inferred across the gap and the case goes to a human.

Conceded as to the two messages (F10, F11), but the record is complete and timestamped (F12), so nothing shows the rider read or replied to either message, and the 14:26 notice came only seconds before the 14:26:55 cancellation (F5) — notice sent is not notice given.

The rider's "a minute after" is from the complaint, not a fact, and my case does not rest on it: the fee fails because the driver's own record cannot carry NS-1(iii) (F1, F7), so on NS-2 there is no completed condition for the $6.61 to stand on
Agreed, and I raise no SAFE point: F10, F11, F14 and F15 contain no threat, intimidation or dangerous-driving content, so SAFE-1 does not apply.

The driver was indeed inside range at the tap (F7), so the NS-2 mismeasurement flag does not attach; but his 90-day record already shows one upheld no-show dispute (F18), so if the fee is refused the repeat criterion for account review is met on its own terms.

Restating my own point for the record: F1's 3 min 20 s gap is longer than 2 minutes and spans the end of the wait, so NS-1(iii) cannot be shown and the case should reach a person — the driver's answer (F4's stationary block) is drawn from the same unsampled window.
Conceded to the extent stated: F7 shows the tap at 14:22:15 with the car 39 m from the pickup, and F2 confirms the closest approach was 15 m at 14:21:50, so NS-1(i) and (ii) hold on the records.

The gap is real (F1, F5) but it is neutral, not adverse: the same gap rule says missing samples are not presumed for either side, and the record still shows the driver stationary 39 m from the pickup for the entire 5 min 0 s from 14:21:55 to the 14:26:55 cancellation (F4) with 5 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m (F3).

The rider asks the judge to treat an inferred gap as defeating the driver, but the rule cuts the other way — a gap is not evidence against the wait; F4 independently places a stationary car 39 m from the pickup across the whole gap window, so NS-1(iii) is met by the system record, not by the driver's account.

We do not need F13: NS-1(iii) is carried by F4 (stationary 14:21:55–14:26:55) and F7 (within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap), so whether the written statement is contradicted is immaterial to the outcome.

The rider's absence of replies (F10, F11, F12) is her own case's problem: the driver sent a timestamped arrival notice at 14:22 and a pre-cancellation notice at 14:26, and the complete, fully timestamped record shows the wait ran its course before he cancelled at 14:26:55 (F5).

The rider's own words are that she came down "a minute after he cancelled" — i.e. after 14:26:55 (F5) — while the driver had been parked 39 m from the pickup since 14:21:55 (F4); presence plus a stationary car at the pickup point for five minutes is precisely the workable wait NS-1(iii) requires.

NS-2 only bites if an NS-1 element fails, and none does; the rider's flip side — asking to flag the driver as a "repeat" — is barred because NS-2 attaches that flag only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup range, which F7 (39 m at tap) rules out.
Profile facts (F17, F18) cannot decide the case, and the only question here is whether NS-1(i)–(iii) are met on the system records — F7, F3 and F4 show they are, so the $6.61 fee stands (F8).
